name: contracts: specify transactional immutable evidence persistence and audit

description.purpose: Immutable, complete manifest for source-scoped producer receipts and normalized observations stored transactionally in the existing Excession SQLite database.
description.limitations: A byte-integrity audit proves relational closure and retained receipt bytes, not that the Git commit exists, the source is authentic, any analyzer executed, or the observation semantics are valid.

schema.name: c_persistence
schema.description: Complete source-scoped snapshot membership, not universal analysis coverage

quality.name: strict_json_schema
quality.description: Validate the versioned manifest against persistence.v1.schema.json and verify sorted unique membership IDs in Rust.

quality.name: transactional_audit
quality.description: Audit all SQLite rows, detect missing/extra/tampered records, preserve raw receipt JSON bytes and roll back failed imports.

quality.name: no_semantic_promotion
quality.description: Independent Git source authentication and producer-semantic correctness require separate qualifying evidence.

context.instructions: Never infer missing relationships as absence or convert self-hashed receipts into execution attestations. Feature acceptance needs independent Rust/native tests.

verifiedStatements.question: What does the snapshot audit establish?
verifiedStatements.answer: Integrity and complete membership of the retained records. It does not authenticate Git source or analyzer conclusions.

constraints.constraint: Do not convert a candidate, generic graph edge or review event into a stronger claim than the producer supplied.
Missing observations with incomplete coverage do not prove that relations are absent.
A self-consistent digest does not attest an independent tool execution or security impact.
